questions.scenario: Your best friend is contesting for School Head Boy/Girl. How do you plan to get them the most votes?

options.text: Walk section to section during lunch breaks, talk face-to-face with every student, and hand out cool handmade badges.
Analyze exactly how many students are in the Commerce, Science, and Arts streams to figure out where your friend is weakest.
Draft a powerful, high-energy speech with a viral punchline that your friend can read out during the morning assembly.
Design the entire game plan—deciding when to release posters, who should give testimonials, and managing the team of friends.

questions.scenario: The backbenchers are planning a 'Mass Bunk' during the last period on a Friday. What is your role in making it happen?

options.text: Physically go to the front-benchers and quiet kids one by one to aggressively persuade them to join so no one gets left behind.
Count exactly how many people have agreed and calculate if we have crossed the safe '75% attendance rule' threshold.
Create a hilarious, highly relatable meme or caption for the class WhatsApp group that makes everyone hyped up for the bunk.
Coordinate the exact timing with other sections and make sure everyone leaves the gate quietly at precisely the same moment.

questions.scenario: You are watching the Lok Sabha election results on TV with Papa. What grabs your attention the most?

options.text: Watching the massive rallies on the news and seeing how local party workers are physically handling the humongous crowds.
Staring at the colorful pie charts, swing percentages, and checking if the exit polls match the actual live seat count.
Listening to the catchy political slogans being played on repeat and judging how impactful they sound.
Analyzing the clever coalition decisions and guessing which regional parties will shake hands to form the next government.

questions.scenario: There is a heated election for the local Resident Welfare Association (RWA) in your colony. How do you help your favorite uncle win?

options.text: Go door-to-door across all blocks, drinking tea with the elders, and asking them about their daily water and parking complaints.
Study the demographics of the society—how many senior citizens, tenants, and families live here—to predict their choices.
Draft a compelling letter detailing the uncle's promises and post it beautifully on the colony's Facebook and WhatsApp groups.
Organize a unified park meeting, inviting the loudest complainers, and strategically introducing the uncle at the perfect moment.

questions.scenario: Your group needs to pick a topic for the 10th standard social science presentation, but everyone is arguing. Your move?

options.text: Take a quick hand-vote right there and use your personal friendships to get the majority to agree with your favorite choice.
Create a mental chart of which topics have scoring potential based on past test papers to guide the decision logically.
Pitch a beautifully titled topic like 'The Digital Revolution in Desi Households' that sounds instantly appealing to the teacher.
Assign sub-topics based on each person's strength and layout a timeline so the project is finished flawlessly before the deadline.

questions.scenario: You want to convince your parents to increase your monthly pocket money. What's your strategy?

options.text: Repeatedly bring it up politely during breakfast, lunch, and dinner, showing them your daily hard work around the house.
Present a clear, itemized breakdown of exactly how much a basic auto-fare, coaching notebooks, and tuition snacks cost now.
Give an emotional, highly moving pitch about independence, responsibility, and how growing up means learning to handle finances.
Wait for a day when Papa is in a stellar mood, use Mummy as your key ally to back you up, and smoothly lock in the deal.

questions.scenario: Your school's cultural fest needs more registrations from other local schools. How do you fix this?

options.text: Form a volunteer squad to visit nearby schools in person, giving high-energy invitations to their student councils.
Check which events had the maximum registrations last year and drop the ones that were totally unpopular to save time.
Design an aesthetic digital poster with an epic theme title and write a description that builds massive curiosity.
Partner with local coaching centers to sponsor the event, ensuring thousands of students see the promotions directly.

questions.scenario: A massive online rumor breaks out that your school is canceling the annual sports day. How do you react?

options.text: Gather your sports teammates and march straight to the PT teacher to verify the ground reality in person.
Track where the message came from and check the official school circular portal to prove it is mathematically a hoax.
Draft a perfectly worded, formal message to broadcast to all class groups, urging everyone to stay calm and ignore fake news.
Advise the student council president to hold an urgent meeting with the vice-principal to request a fast public clarification.

questions.scenario: Your gully cricket team needs to buy a new premium leather bat, but the fund box is completely empty. What do you do?

options.text: Go corner to corner in the mohalla, pitching the idea to all the kids who play, and collecting Rs. 20 from each person.
Calculate the exact contribution needed from active players versus occasional players to keep the collection fair.
Give the team a motivational talk about how this new bat will help us crush the rival society team in the upcoming match.
Convince the local sports shop bhaiya to give you a discount by promising that your entire neighborhood will buy from him.

questions.scenario: What is the best compliment a teacher or group leader can give you after an event?

options.text: 'You are amazing at connecting with people; everyone loves talking to you and listening to what you say.'
'Your predictions and data analysis were spot on; you understand patterns better than anyone else.'
'Your words have magic! You know exactly how to write things that grab attention instantly.'
'You are a master strategist; you see the big picture and know how to move the pieces to win.'

Field_Campaigner.title: The Crowd Connector (Field Campaigner / Ground Mobilizer)
Field_Campaigner.primary_match_text: You are energetic, charismatic, and a total people's person. You thrive when you are on the ground, talking to real people, understanding their everyday problems, and rallying them for a larger cause.
Field_Campaigner.day_in_the_life: Traveling across assembly constituencies, addressing local community gatherings, organizing massive political rallies, and building a loyal network of ground workers.
Field_Campaigner.alternative_match_text: If not in politics, your brilliant human connection and energy make you a perfect fit for Public Relations (PR), Event Management, or Social Work.
Field_Campaigner.roadmap: 11th/12th: Arts/Humanities (Sociology and Political Science are ideal). Degree: BA in Political Science, Sociology, or Social Work (BSW). Next Steps: Start volunteering actively with student unions or political youth wings during college.

Poll_Analyst.title: The Data Prophet (Poll Analyst / Psephologist)
Poll_Analyst.primary_match_text: You look at the world through numbers, graphs, and trends. You don't rely on guesswork or loud voices; you study demographic data and voter math to predict exactly who will win an election.
Poll_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Analyzing thousands of survey responses, creating complex voting swing models, studying historical caste/community voting patterns, and advising news channels or parties on seat projections.
Poll_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your supreme analytical brain and love for trends would also make you a phenomenal Data Analyst, Market Researcher, or Econometrician.
Poll_Analyst.roadmap: 11th/12th: Arts or Commerce with Mathematics/Economics. Degree: BA/B.Sc in Statistics, Economics, or Political Science. Next Steps: Learn data analytics tools (like Python/R) and intern with premium polling agencies or data think-tanks.

Speechwriter.title: The Slogan Sculptor (Speechwriter / Campaign Designer)
Speechwriter.primary_match_text: You are a creative mastermind who understands the immense power of language and imagery. You know exactly what words will make a crowd cheer, what slogans will go viral on WhatsApp, and how a leader should look.
Speechwriter.day_in_the_life: Drafting historical election speeches for top leaders, writing crisp punchlines for television ads, designing campaign posters, and creating viral social media narrative videos.
Speechwriter.alternative_match_text: With your top-tier creative writing and design skills, you would also excel as a Creative Director in Advertising, Journalist, or Scriptwriter.
Speechwriter.roadmap: 11th/12th: Arts/Humanities (Literature, History, or Political Science). Degree: BA in Journalism, Mass Communication, or English Literature. Next Steps: Build a stellar portfolio of political commentary, content creation, or digital design.

Political_Strategist.title: The Campaign Architect (Political Strategist / Campaign Manager)
Political_Strategist.primary_match_text: You are a quiet mastermind who stays behind the scenes, playing high-stakes political chess. You handle the budgets, study the opposition's weaknesses, and tell the political leader exactly what to do to win.
Political_Strategist.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a high-tech war room, coordinating between poll analysts and field teams, deciding candidate ticket distributions, and advising top politicians on policy narratives.
Political_Strategist.alternative_match_text: Your masterful management, negotiation, and system strategy skills would make you an outstanding Management Consultant, Corporate CEO, or IAS Officer.
Political_Strategist.roadmap: 11th/12th: Any stream (Humanities/Arts preferred). Degree: BA in Political Science, Law (5-year Integrated BA LLB), or BBA. Next Steps: Work with premier political consulting firms (like I-PAC, designBoxed) or pursue a Master's in Public Policy/MBA.
